lead: From Gulf hurricanes to tornado season up north, Alabama homes take on water in many ways. DryFlare gets a crew started on water removal and drying.
risk: Gulf hurricanes, spring tornadoes and heavy storm rain
why: Alabama sits between the Gulf of Mexico and the hills of the Appalachians. It gets both tropical rain and violent spring storms. Hurricane Ivan in 2004 and Hurricane Sally in 2020 pushed water into homes from Mobile Bay to Gulf Shores. The April 2011 tornado outbreak tore roofs off across Tuscaloosa and north Alabama. Every open roof let rain inside.

Away from the coast, the risks shift. Summer storms can drop inches of rain in an hour. Red clay soil drains slowly, so water pools by foundations and seeps into crawl spaces. Like neighboring Mississippi, Alabama has many manufactured homes. Their floors soak up water fast.
image_alt: Storm-damaged roof and broken window on a house in the Gulf states
image_caption: After a Gulf hurricane or tornado, a tarp on the roof stops the next rain from making the damage worse.
problems: Baldwin and Mobile counties, coastal condos
Older homes on piers across central Alabama
tips: Before storm season, photograph every room as proof of condition.
Clear the AC drain line each spring. Clogged lines cause many summer leaks.
Keep gutters clear so rain runs away from the house.
Coastal owners who can't get wind cover from a regular insurer can try the Alabama Insurance Underwriting Association.
insurance: Coastal homes in Baldwin and Mobile counties often have a separate hurricane deductible. It is usually a percentage of the home's insured value. Alabama insurers must offer discounts for homes built or re-roofed to the FORTIFIED standard.

faq.q: What should I do first after hurricane water gets into my Alabama home?
faq.a: Once it is safe, shut off power to wet rooms. Take photos and move valuables to a dry room. Tarp roof holes if you can do it safely. Then call DryFlare so drying starts within 24 to 48 hours, before mold grows.

areas: Coastal calls come in from Gulf Shores, Orange Beach, Fairhope and Daphne as well as Mobile.
